svg.title: Three sources, two paths, one index
svg.desc: SQL Server and a Cloudera CDP cluster feed Microsoft 365 Copilot by two routes. The agent-hosted route runs a gRPC connector behind the Microsoft Graph connector agent and never calls Microsoft Graph itself. The direct push route runs console tools that call the Graph external items API themselves. Everything read from CDP passes a Ranger gate first, which decides whether a table or path may be indexed at all or must be left to a live query. Both routes write into one external index that Copilot and Microsoft Search read.

svg.text: A connector supplies a schema and an IPushSource. Only the engine may say an item counted, and only after the write

svg.text: returned — which is what makes it impossible for a failed crawl to advance a watermark.

svg.text: What deliberately does not go into the index

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A row-filtered or masked table is a per-user view of the data, and an index holds one copy — so it is queried live instead.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A file whose groups resolve to no Entra group is skipped, never written with a fallback grant. Fact tables, event streams

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and raw landing zones are analytics assets, not knowledge assets. The catalogue is indexed even when its tables are not.
